__comment: NVisionX Cluster Health Overview (all clusters, per-environment via $datasource). Sourced entirely from kube-state-metrics and node-exporter - both always-on cluster components, not app-specific business metrics - so every panel here should show real data regardless of which services are currently idle/scaled to zero. | 2026-08-28: added a plain-English status banner, a "What's Wrong Right Now" section with always-visible detail tables (crash-looping pods with reason+restarts, Failed-phase pods, not-ready nodes with condition, pending pods with age), and click-through drill-down links from the Nodes Not Ready / Pods Failed / Pods Pending / Restarts KPI tiles to their matching detail table, per manager request for the dashboard to be self-explanatory to non-engineers.
description: Complete cluster health at a glance, in plain language: one status banner up top, then a KPI strip you can click through to see exactly which pod or node is the problem and why.

panels.description: Green = every check below is clean. Red = at least one node, pod, or job needs attention right now — scroll to "What's Wrong Right Now" for specifics.

result.text: ⚠️  ATTENTION NEEDED — see "What's Wrong Right Now" below

targets.expr: (count(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="false"} == 1) OR on() vector(0)) + (count(kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"$namespace", phase="Failed"} == 1) OR on() vector(0)) + (sum(kube_job_status_failed{namespace=~"$namespace"}) OR on() vector(0))

panels.title: Pods Crash-Looping / Erroring (why + restart count)
panels.description: Every pod currently stuck in a bad waiting state, with the real Kubernetes reason and how many times it's restarted. Restart count is the best available proxy for "how long" — kube-state-metrics doesn't expose an exact failure-start timestamp; for the precise duration, check `kubectl describe pod` or cluster Events.

panels.title: Pods in Failed Phase
panels.description: Pods Kubernetes has marked Failed outright (distinct from crash-looping — these have stopped retrying, usually a one-shot Job pod that errored with restartPolicy: Never).

panels.title: Nodes Not Ready — Why
panels.description: Any node currently reporting a real problem condition (memory/disk/PID pressure, or network unavailable). If a node is Not Ready but shows nothing here, check kubelet/network connectivity directly — not every NotReady cause has its own condition.

panels.title: Pods Pending — How Long
panels.description: Pods stuck in Pending, with minutes since creation. kube-state-metrics doesn't expose the scheduler's reason (insufficient resources, no matching node, etc.) — for that, check `kubectl describe pod` or cluster Events.

panels.title: Pods by Phase
panels.description: Live snapshot of every pod's phase across the selected namespace(s).

panels.title: Pod Restarts Over Time
panels.description: Container restarts, 5m windows. Should be flat at zero outside deploys.

panels.title: Top Restarting Pods (last 1h)
panels.description: The pods worth investigating right now.

panels.title: Recent Job Failures
panels.description: Every Job object currently reporting a failed status.

panels.title: Namespace Breakdown
panels.description: One row per namespace: total pods, running, failed, and restarts in the last hour.

title: Cluster Health Overview
